title: Unit 4: Complete Key Vocabulary & Terminology (25 Words) 📚
content: 📌 Welcome Freshmen Students to Communicative English Skills II (EnLa102) - Unit 4! 👋✨ Here is the complete vocabulary list for Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge, prepared in passage-based for study preparation. ─────────────────────────── 1. Indigenous Knowledge (Noun Phrase) • English: Unique, traditional, local knowledge existing within and developed around specific geographic conditions. • Amharic: የሀገር በቀል እውቀት • Synonyms: Traditional wisdom, Local knowledge, Native practices • Antonyms: Western science, Modern technology, External knowledge • Example: Indigenous knowledge provides sustainable solutions to local environmental and agricultural challenges. ─────────────────────────── 2. Persuasive (Adjective) • English: Able to convince someone to believe or do something through sound reasoning. • Amharic: አሳማኝ / አማኝ • Synonyms: Convincing, Compelling, Cogent, Influential • Antonyms: Unconvincing, Weak, Ineffective, Doubtful • Example: The passage presents persuasive arguments for integrating indigenous knowledge into modern development plans. ─────────────────────────── 3. Solidarity (Noun) • English: Unity or agreement of feeling, action, or mutual support among individuals with common goals. • Amharic: አንድነት / መተባበር / ህብረት • Synonyms: Unity, Harmony, Unanimity, Fellowship • Antonyms: Discord, Disunity, Division, Conflict • Example: Indigenous practices foster social solidarity among community members during difficult times. ─────────────────────────── 5. Disparate (Adjective) • English: Fundamentally different or distinct in quality or kind; impossible to compare. • Amharic: በፍጹም የማይመሳሰል / እጅግ የተለያየ • Synonyms: Distinct, Diverse, Dissimilar, Contrastive • Antonyms: Similar, Identical, Alike, Uniform • Example: We live in a disparate world characterized by unequal distribution of wealth and opportunities. ─────────────────────────── 6. Hindering (Verb / Participle) • English: Making it difficult for someone or something to progress, function, or develop. • Amharic: እንቅፋት የሚሆን / የሚያግድ • Synonyms: Impeding, Obstructing, Retarding, Inhibiting • Antonyms: Promoting, Facilitating, Helping, Advancing • Example: Local solutions were wrongly discriminated against as hindering modern economic progress. ─────────────────────────── 7. Anecdote (Noun) • English: A short, informal, or amusing real story about a person or event. • Amharic: አጭር የግል ታሪክ / ወግ • Synonyms: Story, Narrative, Account, Tale • Antonyms: Empirical evidence, Scientific proof, Fact • Example: Critics often argue that a collection of anecdotes does not equal scientific proof. ─────────────────────────── 8. Pertinent (Adjective) • English: Directly relating to or significant to the matter currently being considered. • Amharic: አግባብነት ያለው / የሚመለከት / ጠቃሚ • Synonyms: Relevant, Applicable, Fitting, Suitable • Antonyms: Irrelevant, Inapplicable, Unrelated, Impertinent • Example: The most pertinent issues in local development relate to community ownership and self-reliance. ─────────────────────────── 9. Empowerment (Noun) • English: The process of becoming stronger and more confident, especially in controlling one's life or rights. • Amharic: ማብቃት / አቅም መገንባት • Synonyms: Enablement, Strengthening, Capacity-building, Mobilization • Antonyms: Disempowerment, Weakening, Marginalization • Example: Lasting empowerment comes from within communities rather than being imposed from outside. ─────────────────────────── 10. Self-reliance (Noun) • English: Reliance on one's own capabilities, powers, and resources rather than those of others. • Amharic: በራስ መተማመን / በራስ አቅም መቆም • Synonyms: Independence, Autonomy, Self-sufficiency, Self-direction • Antonyms: Dependence, Reliance, Subservience • Example: Promoting self-reliance enables local communities to solve their own development problems. ─────────────────────────── 11. Prevail (Verb) • English: To prove superior in power or influence; to succeed, survive, or triumph. • Amharic: የበላይነት ማግኘት / ማሸነፍ / መዝለቅ • Synonyms: Triumph, Overcome, Succeed, Persist • Antonyms: Fail, Collapse, Succumb, Yield • Example: Communities that continually learn and adapt to environmental changes will prevail. ─────────────────────────── 12. Camouflage (Verb / Noun) • English: To disguise or hide the true nature, identity, or presence of something. • Amharic: መሸፈን / መደበቅ / ማታለል • Synonyms: Disguise, Mask, Conceal, Cover up • Antonyms: Reveal, Expose, Uncover, Disclose • Example: Paternalistic development programs are sometimes camouflaged by terms like 'capacity strengthening'. ─────────────────────────── 13. Abject (Adjective) • English: Experienced or present to the maximum degree, especially regarding miserable conditions. • Amharic: እጅግ አስከፊ / ዝቅተኛ / አሰቃቂ • Synonyms: Extreme, Wretched, Miserable, Deplorable • Antonyms: Exalted, Prosperous, High, Noble • Example: Modern technology alone has failed to eradicate abject poverty in many developing regions. ─────────────────────────── 14. Substantially (Adverb) • English: To a great, significant, or considerable degree. • Amharic: በከፍተኛ ሁኔታ / በጉልህ / በስፋት • Synonyms: Considerably, Significantly, Greatly, Markedly • Antonyms: Slightly, Marginally, Insignificantly • Example: Both scientists and rural farmers would benefit substantially from mutual collaboration. ─────────────────────────── 15. Discriminate (Verb) • English: To make an unjust or prejudicial distinction against a group, idea, or practice. • Amharic: ማግለል / በበደል መለየት / ልዩነት ማድረግ • Synonyms: Marginalize, Segregate, Sidelight, Bias • Antonyms: Include, Integrate, Treat equally, Favor • Example: Traditional medicinal practices were often unfairly discriminated against as outdated. ─────────────────────────── 16. Constraint (Noun) • English: A limitation or restriction that controls what can be done or achieved. • Amharic: ገደብ / ማቀቢያ / ተጽዕኖ • Synonyms: Limitation, Restriction, Barrier, Curb • Antonyms: Freedom, Liberty, Asset, Advantage • Example: Local communities have coped with environmental challenges despite severe economic constraints. ─────────────────────────── 17. Sustainable (Adjective) • English: Able to be maintained or continued at a stable level without depleting natural resources. • Amharic: ዘላቂ / ጽኑ የሆነ • Synonyms: Viable, Durable, Continuous, Renewable • Antonyms: Unsustainable, Temporary, Short-lived • Example: Building on indigenous knowledge increases the sustainability of development projects. ─────────────────────────── 18. Herbal Medicine (Noun Phrase) • English: The practice of using plants and plant extracts for therapeutic and medicinal purposes. • Amharic: የዕፅዋት ሕክምና • Synonyms: Traditional remedy, Botanical medicine, Phytotherapy • Antonyms: Synthetic drug, Pharmaceutical medicine • Example: Many rural communities rely on herbal medicine as their primary source of healthcare. ─────────────────────────── 19. Remnant (Noun) • English: A small remaining quantity, trace, or piece of something from the past. • Amharic: ቅሪት / የተረፈ • Synonyms: Relic, Remains, Trace, Vestige • Antonyms: Whole, Entirety, Bulk • Example: The fossilized remnants of Lucy prove that early human life originated in Ethiopia. ─────────────────────────── 20. Peculiar (Adjective) • English: Specific, distinct, or unique to a particular group, place, or situation. • Amharic: ልዩ / ያልተለመደ / የተለየ • Synonyms: Particular, Specific, Distinctive, Unique • Antonyms: Orthodox, Common, Normal, Standard • Example: Each indigenous culture possesses peculiar strategies suited to its environmental conditions. ─────────────────────────── 21. Paternalistic (Adjective) • English: Managing or governing individuals or communities in a fatherly manner that restricts freedom or autonomy. • Amharic: አባታዊ / ነጻነትን የሚገድብ አሰራር • Synonyms: Authoritative, Patronizing, Overbearing • Antonyms: Democratic, Empowering, Egalitarian • Example: External aid programs often fail when they adopt a paternalistic approach toward local communities. ─────────────────────────── 22. Marginalize (Verb) • English: To treat a person, group, concept, or practice as insignificant or peripheral. • Amharic: ማግለል / ከዋናው መስመር ማውጣት • Synonyms: Sideline, Ostracize, Exclude, Disregard • Antonyms: Include, Integrate, Mainstream, Promote • Example: Modern development strategies should avoid marginalizing traditional agricultural wisdom. ─────────────────────────── 23. Reciprocity (Noun) • English: The practice of exchanging things, ideas, or support with others for mutual benefit. • Amharic: የጋራ ጥቅም / እርስ በእርስ መረዳዳት • Synonyms: Mutuality, Exchange, Cooperation, Interdependence • Antonyms: Unilateralism, Independence, Antagonism • Example: Successful partnerships between scientists and local farmers depend on mutual respect and reciprocity. ─────────────────────────── 24. Preservation (Noun) • English: The act of keeping something intact, safe, or alive from destruction, decay, or loss. • Amharic: ጥበቃ / መንከባከብ / ጠብቆ ማቆየት • Synonyms: Conservation, Protection, Maintenance, Safeguard • Antonyms: Destruction, Neglect, Loss, Abandonment • Example: The preservation of indigenous knowledge is essential for maintaining biodiversity. ─────────────────────────── 25. Complementary (Adjective) • English: Combining in such a way as to enhance, complete, or emphasize the qualities of each other. • Amharic: እርስ በእርስ የሚሟላ / አጋዥ • Synonyms: Harmonious, Mutual, Interlocking, Integrative • Antonyms: Contradictory, Incompatible, Conflicting • Example: Indigenous practices and modern technology should be viewed as complementary tools for development. ─────────────────────────── ❤️ Dear EthioFresh Students!
